patch_description: Replace the placeholder (all points at origin, giving score 0) with a deterministic optimization: initialize 11 points in the equilateral triangle (vertices plus an interior spread), then run a seeded hill-climbing local search that repeatedly perturbs the vertices of the currently-worst triangle and accepts only improvements to the global minimum triangle area. Points are clipped back into the triangle (y >= 0, y <= √3·x, y <= √3·(1−x)) after every perturbation. The minimum area over all C(11,3)=165 triples is computed vectorized with NumPy, and the RNG is seeded so the output is fully reproducible. This directly maximizes the primary metric (min_area_normalized) while remaining fast (~0.5–1 s) and robust: if anything fails, it returns the last feasible (clipped) configuration, and a pure NumPy fallback grid is used as the initialization.
